You may add a pure retry-budget helper to crates/michi-core/src/resilience.rs as a NEW function/type only (don't touch render_already_done).

Read first: docs/research/pipeline-design.md (the research report — its ranked list of 9 changes is approved by the maintainer), the current crates/michi-pipeline/src/lib.rs and CHANGELOG.md, docs/spec/06-decisions.md (pipeline entries: replay rule, duplicate ids, run state, breaker generations), PRINCIPLES.md (TDD; gates; adopt ecosystem pieces, build only the opinionated agent-facing layer), CLAUDE.md non-negotiables (no unwrap/expect in lib code, every pub item documented, BTreeMap for output maps, divan benches, nextest).

Step 1 — write the spec: docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md (plain concise prose, sentence-case headings, no hard wrapping) describing the new API and semantics, then implement it. Design, adopting the report's ranked changes:
1. Identity: `StepId` and `RunId` newtypes. StepId: caller-chosen readable slug (validate charset/length; reject empty), unique per plan. RunId: caller-supplied (helper to build one; no `uuid` dependency in the default build). Step display `name` is free-form and may repeat.
2. Definition vs run: `ExecStep { id: StepId, name, depends_on: Vec<StepId>, runner: Box<dyn Step> }` (or a builder) forms an immutable `Plan`; validation happens up front and returns ALL violations at once (duplicate ids, unknown deps, self-deps, cycles via iterative Kahn) as a typed error separate from run results; `plan()` / dry-run gives the validated execution order without running. Execution returns a `#[must_use]` `RunRecord` (private fields + accessors): run_id, plan fingerprint over (id, depends_on), per-step terminal status + reason + attempts (with per-attempt replay class) + timing, overall `RunOutcome` that is Succeeded only if every step Completed or CompletedEarlier (never when anything was skipped, not run, unknown or panicked), and root-cause vs consequential failures.
3. Status model (michi-core StepStatus, `#[non_exhaustive]`): Pending, Running, Completed, CompletedEarlier (resume), Failed (ran, definitive), OutcomeUnknown (ambiguous: timeout/502/504/cancelled mid-flight for a non-idempotent step — terminal, agent must verify), Skipped(PrerequisiteFailed | Cancelled-before-start), NotRun(CircuitOpen), Panicked (harness failure, separate from step errors). Update the Pipeline TOON render (and NAPI string mapping/TS types if the pipeline types are exposed) accordingly.
4. Replay: keep the approved replay rule (not-executed / rejected 429,503 / ambiguous timeout,502,504 / definitive), replace the `is_idempotent()` bool with an enum (e.g. `Replay::Idempotent | Replay::NotIdempotent`, default NotIdempotent) on the Step trait; ambiguous outcomes of non-idempotent steps end as OutcomeUnknown and are never auto-replayed; keep `ExecutionError::AmbiguousOutcome` semantics for outward guidance. `StepContext { run_id, step_id, attempt, cancellation (child token), deadline }` with `idempotency_key()` = run_id:step_id (stable across attempts and across resume).
5. Resume: a separate `resume(prior: &RunRecord, plan, opts)` entry point: requires the same RunId and matching plan fingerprint (else typed error), never re-runs Completed/CompletedEarlier steps (they become CompletedEarlier), re-runs Failed/Skipped/NotRun/Pending steps, and treats OutcomeUnknown steps per the replay rule (re-run only if the step is Idempotent; otherwise keep OutcomeUnknown unless the caller explicitly marks them verified via an option). Document at-least-once per step; never claim exactly-once; not incremental recomputation.
6. Scheduling: ONE scheduler loop on tokio::task::JoinSet (scope-owned; nothing outlives execute/resume), `Mode::Sequential` (declaration order, deterministic) and `Mode::Parallel { max_concurrency: NonZeroUsize }` (dispatch ready steps in declaration order while fewer than the cap are running — the cap is enforced in the dispatch loop, not via a semaphore inside spawned tasks); `FailurePolicy::{SkipDependents (default: independent branches keep running, only transitive dependents skip), FailFast (stop dispatching, cancel running via token with a grace period then abort)}`. Panics caught via JoinError → Panicked.
7. Cancellation and time: ADOPT tokio-util's `CancellationToken` (add `tokio-util` dependency, wrap it in michi's own newtype so tokio-util's 0.x type doesn't leak publicly); run-level parent token, per-step child token passed in StepContext; backoff sleeps and attempts race cancellation. Per-attempt timeout (tokio::time::timeout) plus a total per-step deadline across retries.
8. Breakers and budgets: replace the single shared CircuitBreaker with a keyed registry (key chosen by the step, e.g. `Step::breaker_key()` defaulting to the step id or a caller-provided key per downstream service), passable across runs so samples accumulate; keep the existing mutex + generation state machine per key. Add a retry budget (pure helper in michi-core resilience, modelled on tower's TpsBudget: deposit on success, withdraw per retry, ~10% ratio) enforced by the executor.
9. Observability: a per-step completion observer (trait or closure, called synchronously with the step's terminal record) so callers can persist progress and survive a process crash.
Remove the old API (execute_pipeline, execute_pipeline_parallel, StepDependencies, positional runners) — unpublished, no deprecation needed — and update everything that used it (tests, docs, examples, README/ARCHITECTURE mentions, napi if any). Keep the existing breaker generation and replay test coverage, porting tests to the new API; every new behavior gets a red-first test (deterministic with #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]; assert dispatch order, not completion order). Add a divan bench for scheduler overhead at ~500 steps (build-only in CI is fine).

Docs: the new spec 08, update docs/spec/06-decisions.md (new entry "Resolved 2026-10-21 — Pipeline execution redesign" summarizing decisions and what was adopted vs built and why, superseding the "Open" bullet of the replay-rule entry), crates/michi-pipeline/CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased), README/ARCHITECTURE/CLAUDE.md pipeline mentions.

Finish with: `cargo nextest run -p michi-pipeline`, `--all-features`, `cargo nextest run -p michi-core --all-features` (to confirm your core pipeline-module changes), `cargo clippy -p michi-pipeline -p michi-core --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p michi-pipeline --check`, `cargo bench -p michi-pipeline --no-run`, `typos`, markdown check `CI=true pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.oxfmtignore --check "**/*.md"`. Report: the final public API (signatures), each of the 9 changes with its red test and observed failure, adopted crates (version, why), what stayed custom and why, behavior changes, remaining open questions, command results.

The search supports the premise: npm's OIDC trusted publishing can't create a package, so the first release has to be done another way.

- **Why the first publish is manual:** A WordPress Playground doc says the automated workflow can't publish a new package on its first run, because OIDC trusted publishing only applies to packages that already exist and have a trusted publisher configured. When you add a new npm package to the monorepo, the automated release workflow won't be able to publish it on the first run. This is an npm security feature
- **Steps after that:** The same doc says to publish once from a local machine with `npm login` and `npm publish --access public`, then add the trusted publisher in the package's settings on npmjs.com. An npm package must exist before its package-level Trusted Publisher can be configured. One project's release guide uses `npm login --auth-type=web` for that initial login.
- **Matching details:** Trusted publisher fields are checked against your repo. npm's docs say the workflow filename must include the `.yml` or `.yaml` extension, and the file must exist in `.github/workflows/`. Enter only the filename, not the full path. A WordPress doc notes the fields are case-sensitive.
